messages:
incident-bot: Paging on-call: Dedicated pool valen-prod-1 reports >25% pod restarts in the canary slice. Severity: P2. @oncall-night please acknowledge.

oncall-night: Acked. Pulling logs now. Anyone with Valen account pinged.

sara_nguyen: Seeing a sharp increase in kernel OOM events on gpus-07 in valen-prod-1 canary. GC looks fine. Repro on a synthetic traffic replay.

jamal_khan: Is the canary still serving traffic? Traffic shift was 10% last hour.

eva_ops: Canary marked healthy in control-plane but metrics show 10s tail latency spike and memory climbs steadily. Suggest pause rollout and pin artifact.

incident-bot: Action triggered: canary-rollout-policy -> pause; artifact pin requested for revision r2026-04-valen-3.

tom_hayes: I'm on the pool. Running tenant isolation script to move Valen tenants off the canary nodes. Command: 
```
./scripts/evacuate_tenant.sh --tenant valen-main --pool valen-prod-1 --drain
```
Logs: starting drain, cordon nodes gpus-07,gpus-08.

valen_se: We're on standby. Customer reports some 5xxs in their ingested logs at 14:27 UTC. They asked for ETA; will need a quick mitigation.

jamal_khan: Recommend diverting Valen traffic to fallback pool valen-prod-2 (older artifact r2026-02) while we investigate. That keeps SLA intact.

oncall-night: Initiating routing override in traffic-router. Patch: 
```
POST /admin/route_override
{"tenant":"valen-main","target_pool":"valen-prod-2","reason":"canary-memory-leak-evacuation"}
```
Will monitor.

incident-bot: Routing override applied. Valen traffic now 100% -> valen-prod-2.

sera_nguyen: (typo of sara) Sorry, new info: OOMs correlate with model kv-cache growth when sequence length > 6k in inference path. Canary variant loads a larger context encoder.

eva_ops: Ok that explains memory. We'll roll back the canary config (context_size=8192 -> 4096) and re-run canary later. But first we should freeze artifacts so no auto-rollforward picks r2026-04.

infra-runbook-bot: Runbook: Dedicated pool emergency pin: `runbook/dedicated_pool_pin.md` step 2 -> `./admin/pin_artifact --pool valen-prod-1 --artifact r2026-03`

tom_hayes: Pin applied: artifact r2026-03 pinned for valen-prod-1. Confirmed: control-plane shows pinned=true.

jamal_khan: I will open a high-priority support ticket for Valen and post the mitigation steps. Valen-SE, can you inform the customer now that traffic is diverted and we're evacuating nodes?

valen_se: Confirmed to customer: "We've routed traffic to a stable pool and are isolating your workload while we fix the canary. You'll see decreased error rate within a few minutes." They asked for CC on postmortem.

oncall-night: Evacuation completed: all valen pods terminated on valen-prod-1 canary nodes, no further restarts observed. Memory pressure cleared.

incident-bot: Monitoring: 5xx rate for Valen fell from 6.2% -> 0.8% following reroute. Latency normalized to baseline.

sara_nguyen: Next steps: 1) revert canary config to context_size=4096 and run a small synthetic smoke (5k seq). 2) run extended memory soak at 25% traffic. 3) re-evaluate kernel memory metrics.

jamal_khan: Post-incident assignments: sara -> root cause reproducer and PR for config guard; tom -> automate tenant-evacuate for dedicated pools; oncall-night -> update incident timeline in ops-docs.

valen_se: Customer requested weekly sync and permanent cap on context_size for valen tenant until we validate memory profile. We'll draft SOC/contract note.

eva_ops: I'll schedule a canary retry with reduced context_size after we create a canary runbook entry. For now marking incident resolved from operations perspective.

incident-bot: Incident state -> Mitigated. Please add follow-up tasks and file an RCA within 3 business days.

jamal_khan: Thanks team. I'll kick off RCA doc and set a follow-up meeting with Valen + Eng next Tue.

oncall-night: Handing back to regular oncall at 04:00 UTC. Leaving notes in #eng-oncall.

sara_nguyen: Logging full stack traces and sample requests to S3 at s3://redwood-ops/valen/1758009999/ for RCA.

valen_se: Customer acknowledged and appreciated quick action. Closing their immediate support thread.

tom_hayes: Linking runbook PR: https://git.redwood/repo/infra/runbooks/pull/427

jamal_khan: End of thread.
